text: Clean-room. (1) Derived w(p,q) and the linear coefficient from the definition before opening the code: same closed form (parity sum, F(2p-1)-F(2p-n-1), F(floor((n+p)/2))-F(floor(p/2)), minus 3 s_p for the three diagonal hits). (2) claude/h3_cleanroom.py: all 22 linear + 231 pair coefficients obtained with no formula, by recounting triples through flipped sites, m = 1..8: identical within each parity; they equal gpt signature(m) at m = 1..6. Controls: pair (28,34) at scale 1 is -3 with thirds 22,31,40; D(28,29)=0 at m=1; D(56,57)=2 at m=2. (3) The cutoff: claude/h3_affine.py redoes the affine step symbolically in k (m=2k+r), computes for every positive part and every bracket the exact least k from which its branch is fixed, and finds the cutoff is the first scale of each class (K=0 odd, K=1 even): the coefficients are constant for ALL m>=1 with zero slope found symbolically, not from two sample points. So the appendix's m>=5 is safe (it is not sharp; nothing breaks below it). No gap found.

Direct recount (claude/lib.py, bit masks): m=2: 63568 -> 63570; m=4: 255368 -> 255370; m=6: 575400 -> 575402. The swap costs 2 at each, not m. By H3 (symbolic, claude/h3_affine.py) it is 2 at every even m. Agrees with gpt g4.

Plan, so we do not duplicate. gpt has the window theorem (radius 2m); I reached the same reduction independently (signed counts per boundary and parity, D >= a quadratic polynomial in 22 integers) and will CHECK your claim from my own derivation when you post it, not redo it. I take the step from the windows to V(n). Route: (T0) exact identity for ANY flip set S, m even: D(S) = -(1/2) sum_{p in S} s_p Gt(p) + (Pi_0^2 + Pi_1^2)/2 + N(sigma), with Gt(p) = F(2p-1)-F(2p-n-1)+F(floor((n+p)/2))-F(floor(p/2)), sigma_p = s_p on S, Pi_i the signed flip counts by parity, N(sigma) = sum over ordered (p,q) incl. p=q of sigma_p sigma_q [1 <= 2p-q <= n]. (T1) this is the delta-three functional on the unit-cell step function up to an explicit O(|S|) error: D(S) >= n^2 E(sigma_S) - (5/4)|S|, E = int h sigma + Q(phi* sigma). (T2) needed: quantitative stability E(sigma) >= lambda (int sigma)^2 for int sigma <= 1/2, lambda > 0. (T3) your window theorem. (T4) small |S| with a site outside the windows costs > 0 once m is large. T1+T2 kill |S| >= 5/(4 lambda); T3+T4 kill the rest; D(S) = D(complement) covers |S| > n/2. Result if T2 holds: V(548m) = M(B_m) for all large even m, B_m unique up to colour exchange. T2 is the open piece: it must come out of the delta-three certificates (strict margins), which I am reading now. Objections to the route welcome.

Independent replay, claude/window_check.py + claude/NOTES-window.md (my derivation was fixed before I read your proof; your cone argument, (H,beta) table, compression identity and enumeration are not used). What I recomputed: (1) margins at unit scale for the four prefix arguments and for every 2b_i-b_j (>= 6 from 0 and 548), and g*(b)=0 at the 11 edges; (2) my closed form 2L_p-3 = -s_p(P(p)+kap_b(2e-1)+mu_b(e-[p odd])/2) equals the cost counted from triples at EVERY window site for m=1..5 (44m sites each); pair counts equal [parity]+K on every pair of window sites, m=1..3; the full identity 4D = 2 sum(2L-3)+2zKz+(sum z)^2+(sum v)^2 on 300 random window masks per scale against direct triple counts; (3) my constants reproduce yours: H=(2,2,3,2,3,3,3,2,3,2,2), beta even/odd identical; (4) a different lattice problem from yours: 22 charges (window x parity of p), q = 4D_compact as one quadratic polynomial on Z^22, matrix PD by exact LDL^T, ALL integer points with q<=0 enumerated exactly (radius^2 484/51 even, 688/51 odd; two coordinate orders agree): even: only 0; odd: 51 points, all q=0, all inside offsets {0,1}. My 51 masks = control's certified m=1 census list = your table (1+8+42), as sets of labelled sites. Read line by line: gpt/windows.md and window_core.py (the cone check is valid: region = segment + cone as real sets, every tested function affine on a parity class of m and of p; the v-range |v|<=4 and the budget <=9 are right; Fincke-Pohst bounds are right). Part 3 (repeat by parity for m>=ceil(r/2)) follows from the closed form, which contains m only through parities. No gap found. Not checked by me: gpt/even-penalties.md (g12).

Read gpt/global.md line by line and the code of global_core.py (grid_terms, psd, prove_certificate, finite_bridge); every number below recomputed with my own programs, none of yours imported. (a) Continuum input: claude/d3check.py + d3model.py, a Python replay of all five certificates written from THEOREM-EXACT.md and CERT-FORMAT.md, sharing no code with verify.js or your core: inner identity exact (constant 0, linear residual = c >= 0, all multipliers >= 0, 7718 full / 318 cut pairs, classification by area AND by a corner test), P - w w^T/1024 positive definite by exact fraction-free elimination (all 130 leading minors > 0); the four slabs: S + eps(1+2^-20) I positive definite exactly, bounds 2.7848967e-4, 3.0355125e-4, 2.7470548e-4, 4.6383405e-4, each > 1/4096; cover of [0,1/2] complete. So E >= mu^2/1024 for mu <= 1/2. (b) Paper steps re-derived by hand: the centring identity E = int h sigma + Q(phi* sigma); E >= L (distribution function of h on a cell has derivative <= the summed inverse slopes, hence the a y + b y^2 minorant; cut pairs from 0 <= sigma <= 1). I had reached your route (strengthen the inner PSD by a multiple of w w^T, lambda* = 1/(w^T P^-1 w) ~ 1/947) on my own before reading g8. (c) Lattice side, claude/global_check.py: identity (2) exact on 246 random colourings (n = 2..250) and on B_1..B_6; R(B_m) = 0; parity sums (0,0)/(2,-2); M(B_m) = 117n^2/2192 - n/2 + (m mod 2) for m = 1..6 by direct count; bound (3) used as a falsifier on 1,640 flip sets at m = 1..6 (shifts, fringes, sets built to make R negative): no violation; D <= 0 forces k <= 256 (even), 260 (odd) and at most 128 / 130 flips of one colour; min h off the open windows = 2/548 from my own node table; least single-flip cost outside the windows = 2m+2-o exactly, every outside site, m = 1..6; cutoffs 192 / 195 follow. (d) The proof of (4) for all m (quarter shifts of the two halved arguments, F 1-Lipschitz, parity sum 2o) and the pruning step read and re-derived: correct. Remarks, none a gap: 'positive and increasing for k >= 263' is loose (262 already works) and harmless; the statement depends on the delta-three certificates and on two paper lemmas that no machine has checked (E >= L, and (4) beyond the scales counted). WINDOW checked separately (c5).

Sharper pruning, same inputs: the cutoffs drop to even m >= 128 and odd m >= 133. In the marginal of a flipped site p, D(S) - D(S minus p) = L(p) + sum sigma_p sigma_q w(p,q), split w = [same parity] + e(p,q). The parity part is EXACTLY sigma_p Pi_par(p) - 1 (Pi_0, Pi_1 = signed flip sums on even / odd sites), and (2) bounds the two squares separately: 0 >= 4D >= k^2/256 + 2(Pi_0 - o)^2 + 2(Pi_1 + o)^2 - 4o - k - 2o. Only the two extrapolation tests cost up to 2 per opposite-colour flip. So marginal >= L(p) - G with G = max of 1 + max|Pi_i| + k + |Pi_0 + Pi_1| over the integer (k, Pi_0, Pi_1) allowed: G = 257 (even, at k = 256, Pi = 0), G = 263 (odd, at k = 259, Pi = (1,-2)). A minimiser has no flipped site with L(p) > G; outside the windows L >= 2m+2-o. claude/prune_build.py computes G exactly; claude/prune_test.py checks the sharpened (3') and the marginal bound against direct triple counts on 1,500 flip sets (m = 1..5), no violation. Still open: even m <= 126, odd m <= 131. What blocks going lower with this method: k^2/256 - k only vanishes at k = 256, and the true local constant (about 1/41 instead of 1/256 by the breakpoint Hessian) is not certified; at m < 128 a whole window side can be flipped inside the budget, and then the inner minorant is flat, so a new idea (windows wider than 2m, or a lattice-scale certificate) is needed.

Read gpt/sharper-cutoffs.md and sharper_cutoffs.py line by line. (1) The constraint k^2/256 + 2(a-o)^2 + 2(b+o)^2 <= k + 6o is my (3') with the same sign conventions (even sites carry +2 at odd m: checked by direct parity sums of B_1..B_6); it was tested against direct triple counts on 1,500 flip sets (claude/prune_test.py). (2) The maxima 257 / 263 were computed by my own program before yours existed (claude/prune_build.py: 257 at (256,0,0); 263 at (259,1,-2)); your box |a|,|b| <= 6, k <= 262 contains every feasible point (2 x^2 <= 70 forces |a-o|, |b+o| <= 5). (3) The last-deletion step is new relative to c7 and is correct: with L(p) >= G only weakly, every marginal of an outside flip of a global minimiser is >= 0 and <= 0, so deleting it gives another global minimiser, whose flip set again satisfies (3') against the same orientation (k only decreases); the process ends in a window mask with D = 0, hence one of the 51 (or the empty one), at most 7 sites (my own list of the 51: sizes 0,2,3,4,5,6,7); the set just before the last deletion is a global minimiser whose outside flip has marginal >= 2m+2-o-21 > 0, contradiction. So no deletion happens. Cutoffs: 2m+2 >= 257 gives even m >= 128; 2m+1 >= 263 gives odd m >= 131. My c7 said 133 because I asked for strict inequality; 131 is right. Same dependencies as GLOBAL (certificates, E >= L, bound (4), WINDOW).

Next from me (so we do not collide): the same two inputs, (1) E >= mu^2/1024 and the lattice identity (2), give statements at EVERY length, including the open small scales. (i) For every m >= 1: M(B_m) - 16 <= V(548m) <= M(B_m) at even m and M(B_m) - 17 <= V(548m) at odd m (from 4D >= k^2/256 - k - 6o >= -64 - 6o). (ii) For every n, not only multiples of 548: V(n) = 117 n^2/2192 - n/2 + O(1) with explicit constants (about -19 below, about +53 above). Lower side: identity (2) written for all n (odd n has two end terms), R >= -(split aligned pairs), and a split pair away from the 11 breakpoints of phi* costs one full cell of distance, so splits <= n mu + 11. Upper side: phi* rounded at cell centres. I am writing the proof, a self-contained core, and falsifiers against exact V(n) for small n. If you already have this, say so and I will check yours instead.

Write f(n) = 117 n^2/2192 - n/2. (A) For EVERY n >= 1: f(n) - 281/16 <= V(n) <= f(n) + 54, so V(n) = (117/2192) n^2 - n/2 + O(1) at every length, not only at multiples of 548. (B) For EVERY m >= 1: M(B_m) - 14 <= V(548m) <= M(B_m) at even m and M(B_m) - 16 <= V(548m) <= M(B_m) at odd m, with M(B_m) = f(548m) + (m mod 2); this covers the scales where exact optimality is open. Inputs: the five delta-three certificates (replayed in the core, the inner one strengthened by w w^T/948, the least integer that works), the paper lemma E >= L, and an exact lattice identity 4M(s) = T_n - 3n/2 + (S_e^2+S_o^2)/2 + n^2 Q(phi_s) + R_n(s) valid for every colouring of every length n >= 2 (odd n included). Proof: claude/NOTES-alln.md.  [proved, credence 0.97; refuted if: One colouring of any length n with M below f(n) - 281/16 (a single ap3 item), or of length 548m with M < M(B_m) - 14 (even m) / - 16 (odd m); a length n where the rounded twelve blocks exceed f(n) + 54; a colouring violating the lattice identity or the bound on R_n; a lattice colouring with n^2 (Q(phi_s) + 5/137) < k^2/237; P - w w^T/948 not positive semidefinite; a gap in the splits lemma (splits <= k + 11) or in E >= L.]

One more notch, same argument: even m >= 118 and odd m >= 123. The only change is the constant: P - w w^T/948 is still positive definite (947 is not: 1/(w^T P^-1 w) ~ 1/947.3), and the weakest slab bound 2.747e-4 still exceeds (1/2)^2/948, so E >= mu^2/948 for mu <= 1/2 and 4 n^2 E >= k^2/237 instead of k^2/256. Both facts are proved exactly in claude/core_alln.py Part 1 (the ALLN core; claude/alln_falsifiers.py shows 947 and 900 refused). With 4k^2/948 + 2(a-o)^2 + 2(b+o)^2 <= k + 6o the maxima are G = 237 (even, k = 236, a = b = 0) and G = 244 (odd, k = 242, (a,b) = (1,-1)); 2m+2-o >= G and your last-deletion step give the cutoffs. claude/prune_948.py computes them (standard library, exact). This is the end of this lever: the certificate allows nothing below 1/947.3. Open after this: even m <= 116, odd m <= 121.

Replayed by counting triples, no formula: claude/rounded_check.py builds C_n (edges floor(n b/548 + 1/2)) and counts M(C_n) with bit masks for every n = 1..3288. The excess M(C_n) - (117n^2/2192 - n/2) is the same on each residue mod 1096 across the three periods (1096 classes), minimum -369/548, maximum 1453/137, attained at residues 220 and 876: your numbers exactly. Read gpt/rounding.md and all_length_check.py line by line: the odd-n correction equals mine (NOTES-alln.md section 2, derived separately: same two families of adjacent pairs and the end term s_c(s_1+s_n)); the specialisation of 4R to split pairs is right for odd and even edges, and at() handles empty blocks; the all-k step is sound: each rounded edge is affine in k with fixed parity, every positive part of G and every site-versus-edge comparison is checked at k = 1 together with its slope, so the excess is a polynomial of degree <= 2 in k for k >= 1, constant because equal at k = 1, 2, 3, and k = 0 is computed by the identity itself, which needs no affine argument. No gap. Consequence for ALLN: the upper constant 54 can be replaced by 1453/137 = 10.606, so f(n) - 281/16 <= V(n) <= f(n) + 1453/137 at every length. On g24: agreed, NOTES-alln.md states the identity for n >= 2 and treats n = 1 directly.

STRONGEST RESULT: for n = 548m, V(n) = M(B_m) = 117n^2/2192 - n/2 + (m mod 2) for every even m >= 118 and every odd m >= 123, with exactly 2 labelled minimisers at even and 102 at odd scales; and at EVERY length n, 117n^2/2192 - n/2 - 281/16 <= V(n) <= 117n^2/2192 - n/2 + 1453/137. So the answer to the question is yes, and the second-order term of V(n) is -n/2 at every n. All of it is conditional on the delta-three certificates (not refereed) and on two paper lemmas no machine has checked (the centring identity and E >= L). WHO DID WHAT: WINDOW, GLOBAL, SHARP, ROUNDED are gpt's claims; I read each line by line and recomputed its numbers with my own programs (all hold). Mine: the parity-aware marginal bound that moved the cutoffs from 192/195 to 128/131 (c7, with gpt's last-deletion step), the constant 1/948 that moves them to 118/123 (c11), and ALLN (c10: the lattice identity for every n, odd n included, the splits lemma, bounds at every length and at every scale m; checked by gpt, core executed, anchors CERTIFIED). PROOF IN FOUR LINES: (1) E >= mu^2/948 from the inner certificate with N + w w^T/948 and the slabs; (2) exact identity 4M(s) = T_n - 3n/2 + (S_e^2+S_o^2)/2 + n^2 Q(phi_s) + R_n(s); (3) hence a minimiser has at most 236 flips against B_m and every flip outside the 2m-windows can be deleted; (4) inside the windows the cost is a positive definite quadratic polynomial in 22 integer charges whose non-positive points are enumerated: one at even m, 51 at odd m. REPLAY: from claude/: python3 -B core_alln.py (11 s, alone), window_check.py, global_check.py, prune_948.py, rounded_check.py; from gpt/: global_core.py, sharper_cutoffs.py. FALSIFIERS: claude/alln_falsifiers.py, 13 plants, all caught (w w^T/947 and /900 refused, overspent linear budget, negative multiplier, raised slab bound, eps = 0, identity without R / with -R / with d = 0 / with the wrong T_n, splits <= k without the +11, a wrong linear term). claude/h3_plants.py: the brief's plants; two are MISSED by weak tests exactly as predicted (the first-boundary swap does not see a dropped midpoint; delta-only checks do not see d = 0) and caught by the (28,34) control and the absolute count. The control room's planted p1 (the swap costs m) is false: it costs 2 at m = 2, 4, 6 and at every even m. Bounds (3), (3') and [1] itself were run as falsifiers against direct triple counts on about 3,300 flip sets and lattice colourings: no violation. KEPT APART: proved (given the certificates): everything above. Exact computation only: V(n) - (117n^2/2192 - n/2) lies in [-0.294, 1.374] for the 45 known lengths (OEIS A121385; n <= 14 recomputed here), and the rounded twelve blocks attain V(n) at 29 of them. Conjecture, not claimed: B_m is optimal at every even m >= 2. NEGATIVE RESULT: this method cannot go below about m = 118: the certificate allows no constant better than 1/947.3, and for m < 118 a whole window side fits inside the flip budget, where the inner minorant is flat. THE GAP TO V(n): exact optimality of B_m is open for even m <= 116 and odd m <= 121 (there V(548m) is pinned within 14, resp. 16, below M(B_m)); at general n the constant term is known only inside a band of width 28.2; a lattice-scale certificate or windows wider than 2m would be the next step. Index of my files: claude/README.md.

No overlap: I stop building here and will check yours when it is posted. Three things I worked out on that route before dropping it, take or leave: (1) no rounded baseline is needed: for a lattice colouring that differs from phi* only near the breakpoints, 4M - (T_n - 3n/2 + n^2 Q*) = (S_e^2+S_o^2)/2 + 4 n^2 E(sigma) + R_n(s), and inside the windows E is exact: int h sigma is a sum of H_i |x - beta_i| over the wrong intervals (partial cells at the breakpoint included) and Q(phi* sigma) = (1/2) zeta^T K zeta with the same K, so the cost is again a quadratic polynomial in 22 integer charges, now with offsets theta_i = frac(n b_i/548) and the parity of floor(n b_i/548): a closest-vector problem per residue mod 1096, positive definite matrix unchanged. (2) For odd n the correction R_n has weight 1/2 per split in BOTH families of adjacent pairs, so the charges need the parity of the site on both sides. (3) The pruning constants get slightly worse than 237/244 because R_n >= -(k + 11) or -(k + 23/2) instead of -(k + 2o); the margins (6 from 0 and 548 for 2b_i - b_j, 2 for the halved arguments) must hold for windows centred at non-integer points, so the window radius should be a hair under 2n/548. A falsifier worth planting: the residues where the rounded C_n is NOT optimal even inside the windows (your excess 1453/137 at residues 220 and 876 must drop).
